editorial:
You follow two fourteen-year-old friends, Megan and Amy, who spend hours online, posting videos and chatting with strangers. Their world feels normal at first, but the movie slowly shows how easy it is for a predator to slip into that space. The found-footage style makes everything feel close and uncomfortable, like you are watching real clips instead of a polished film. It is not a fun horror movie; it is a heavy drama that wants to warn you about online danger and how fast trust can turn into fear.

The acting feels raw, especially from the young cast, and the pacing builds dread without rushing. The downside is that the final stretch is extremely upsetting and hard to watch, so this is not for everyone. If you can handle dark true-crime stories, it may stick with you for days. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or pick up the 4K Blu-ray. Watch with care, and maybe not alone at night.
endingExplained: In the final video, Amy has been kidnapped and is trapped in a barrel while Josh films her. She begs for help and says she wants her mom, but Josh tells her he is going to bury her. The footage ends as dirt is poured over her, confirming that both Megan and Amy are dead and that the online stranger was a predator all along.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark found-footage thrillers and can handle intense subject matter.
